title: Pell Smells Sandbagging
warm:
Marcus Pell smelled sandbagging the way Crownspire smelled money—before the words finished forming. Controlled drip had been [player_name]'s method: partial calendar truths, soft neighbor answers, Rhea Quinn tipped just enough to slow slate access without inventing a corpse. Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rose without a body. Vivienne's four fates stayed contested. Nolan Greer stood mid-forties with cufflinks patient and brutal charm carefully sheathed while his fixer inventoried the soft alibi for leaks.

"You are metering," Pell said in the penthouse glass hush. "Brooks can feel the sand in the bag. Holding boards hate sand. Reconstruct the last hour cleanly—or retreat across the hall and pretend geography is innocence."

[player_name]—early thirties, she/her, neighbor-mistress—tasted oak and insult. Soft was pliable evidence; Pell wanted steel. Unused perfume still breathed. Black car curb-idle. Elevator chime. Wind sheer throwing city light as accusation. Weekly to monthly to gone still underlined nowhere as settled death.

Nolan's glance said protection had a lawyer-shaped price. "If you reconstruct the last hour with him, you hand Pell a script Brooks might later seize. If you cross the hall, you keep drip control and look like flight to anyone watching cameras."

She catalogued controlled drip's remaining give: not enough to satisfy Brooks, too much to please Pell, exactly enough to keep Vivienne's fate L10-open. Choice verbs waited—reconstruct, or retreat across the hall into the soft alibi's private weather.

Hope and dread shared the wine ring. Soft sandbagging had a scent now, and Pell had named it aloud.

Controlled drip had begun as mercy and aged into tactic. [player_name] had given Brooks dinners that sounded ordinary, elevator nights that sounded empty, and calendar edges that stopped short of the unnamed hour. Pell's binder preferred total inventory; Brooks's notebook preferred corpses; Nolan preferred her soft enough to keep both predators guessing. Soft alibi sandbagging was the ugly word for surviving between those hungers without settling Vivienne as willing, paid, dead, or staging.

She walked once past the wine ring, past the bath corridor's perfume ghost, back to the fixer who smelled metering the way Crownspire smelled rain on glass. "If I reconstruct the last hour, I hand you a script that can be seized. If I cross the hall, I keep the drip and look like flight on every lobby camera Rhea pretends not to watch."

Nolan's cufflinks stayed still—rare mercy. "Both keep Brooks warmer. Neither invents a body. Soft still fits your mouth; Pell wants to know if it still fits his paperwork."

Across the hall waited clearer conscience and colder sheets. Here, sandbagging had been named, and naming made the next verb cost more. Elevator chime. Black car. Wind sheer. Hope and dread shared the hour like co-authors who refused to sign.

Nolan's cufflink tick traveled her spine. "Reconstruct the last hour for him—or walk across the hall and keep your private throb out of his binder." His eyes promised later hands either way. Mid-want pooled. She clenched around the choice.

Elevator chime. Wind sheer. Black car. Soft alibi pulse between throat and cunt. Romance locked on Nolan alone. She trembled choosing which verb kept her hunger from becoming Pell's exhibit.

She felt Pell's audit like hands that were not Nolan's and wanted Nolan's anyway. Soft alibi eroticism under fixer scrutiny stayed body-true: pulse at throat, heat low, silk clinging, mid-want refusing to resolve while Vivienne stayed contested.
